# How Stylists Manufacture Cultural Meaning — finished platform kit

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Open on one garment alone, then add body, accessory, setting, pose, crop, caption, and distribution one layer at a time. Name the decision-maker only where the record does. Close by separating interpretation from ownership.

## 2. SHORT 01
“A garment does not enter culture alone.” Reveal six relational decisions in forty-five seconds; finish on the missing-credit test.

## 3. SHORT 02
“Credit is not a license. Approval is not authorship. Visibility is not payment.” Pair each distinction with the record that would evidence it.

## 4. CAROUSEL
Object; body; relation; reference; frame; caption; contract; correction. Each frame asks one question and names one evidence field.

## 5. AUDIO
A six-minute assistant-to-lead handoff: selections, refusals, cultural references, permissions, returns, and unresolved credit.

## 6. CLASSROOM
Restyle one public-domain fashion plate three ways, disclose every choice, and compare meanings without claiming new facts about the original.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** FIT describes stylists as developing visual brand and design concepts that guide work toward a finished product. (S82)
- **VERIFIED:** FIT’s Women of Harper’s Bazaar exhibition framed fashion publishing as collaboration among an editor, fashion editor, and photographer rather than the product of a single role. (S83)
- **INFERENCE:** A styling choice can shape public meaning without automatically establishing copyright ownership, contractual approval, or sole authorship. (S53, S54, S82, S83)

## Publication discipline
Do not invent production arrangements or add unlicensed imagery. Preserve captions, alt text, creator and institution credits, canonical URLs, evidence labels, labor and jurisdiction limits, participant correction, and counsel or specialist gates.
